description: The bar chart illustrates the difference in average Word Error Rate (WER) from the Whisper large model when various text preprocessing optimisations are applied, comparing performance between two fine-tuned models: NESAC ft model (brown bars) and SESHA ft model (green bars). The vertical axis lists five optimisation categories — “Normalised”, “Add Spacing”, “Remove Spacing”, “Americanisms”, and “Dates” — arranged from top to bottom. The horizontal axis represents the “Difference in Average WER from Whisper large”, scaled from 0.000 to approximately 0.0035, with tick marks at 0.000, 0.001, 0.002, and 0.003. For each optimisation, two adjacent horizontal bars show the WER difference for each model, with exact values labeled at the end of each bar. The NESAC ft model consistently shows slightly higher WER differences than the SESHA ft model across all categories. For example, under “Normalised”, NESAC ft has a WER difference of 0.00334 versus 0.00323 for SESHA ft; under “Dates”, NESAC ft shows 0.00257 versus 0.00228 for SESHA ft. The “Normalised” optimisation yields the highest WER difference for both models, while “Dates” yields the lowest. The chart visually suggests that SESHA ft generally performs closer to Whisper large than NESAC ft under these text preprocessing conditions.
